newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.

text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division on Friday and Saturday (league positions in parenthesis):

With leaders Bayern Munich and second-placed VfB Stuttgart clashing on Sunday, defending champions Dortmund have a great chance to go top. Dortmund playmaker Andy Moeller may miss game (calf injury) and their striker Heiko Herrlich also may not start because of bruised calf. Defender Juergen Kohler also suspended for home team. Hamburg are without Austrian defender Markus Schopp (suspended). Dortmund unbeaten for last six games. Hamburg have not won there since 1987-88 season.
St. Pauli expected to be unchanged after 3-1 defeat of title challengers Bayer Leverkusen last week. Bochum without midfielder Peter Peschel (stomach muscle pull).

Moenchengladbach struggling with long list of injuries including Swedish striker Martin Dahlin, defender Hubert Fournier and midfielder Stephan Passlack. Duisburg likely to keep with much of team which upset Stuttgart 3-1 last weekend.
Both teams are threatened with relegation and need points. Bielefeld are confident after three consecutive victories, Rostock in trouble after three defeats and a poor record at home.
Swiss midfielder Alain Sutter returns for Freiburg after hip injury. Czech midfielder Jiri Nemec is suspended for Schalke.
Karlsruhe are missing their most important player, Germany midfielder Thomas Haessler, who faces long layoff with broken ankle. 1860 have not won for five games. Karlsruhe unbeaten for three games.
Bremen need to bounce back from 4-0 home defeat by Dortmund last weekend. Werder have not won for four games but Duesseldorf have the worst home record in the Bundesliga.

Fascinating Rhineside derby with both clubs making a bid for the championship. Leverkusen have good home record, winning five of their seven games, but Cologne have won three out of seven away matches.
